downtown:
Market Insight · Downtown Peninsula: Downtown, Yaletown, Coal Harbour & West End

Downtown Peninsula Market

The Downtown Peninsula is really four condo markets, each with its own personality. Downtown is the tower core around Granville, Robson and the business district. Yaletown pairs its converted brick warehouses and patios along Mainland and Hamilton with the marina-side neighbourhoods on False Creek, where towers and townhomes sit right on the seawall. Coal Harbour is the quieter waterfront edge, with marina and floatplane views and the highest benchmark price of the four. The West End is the most residential, with leafy blocks, character walk-ups and newer towers between Stanley Park and English Bay. Each moves at its own pace, so we track them side by side. Here’s where values are heading, how quickly homes are selling and how much room buyers have to negotiate, updated every month from Greater Vancouver REALTORS® data.

Mount Pleasant Market

Mount Pleasant is one of Vancouver’s oldest neighbourhoods, and you can feel it: heritage houses and older low-rises on the side streets, with a newer wave of condos closer to Main and Broadway. The area grew up around Brewery Creek, and today’s craft breweries along Main, plus the murals that go up every summer, keep that spirit going. Condos and townhouses make up most of the sales here, so that’s what we track. Grandview-Woodland Market

Grandview-Woodland is the multicultural heart of East Van, built around Commercial Drive. The Drive is Vancouver’s Little Italy, with a strong Portuguese thread as well, so you get old-school espresso bars, Italian delis, patios and live music, along with a counter-culture streak that’s never really left. The side streets mix grand old character homes with older low-rise apartments, so we track houses, condos and townhouses. Market Insight · Strathcona

Strathcona Market

Strathcona is Vancouver’s oldest residential neighbourhood, a few blocks from Chinatown and Gastown, with colourful restored heritage houses, front porches and community gardens. It’s long been a landing place for newcomers and a home for artists, and it’s kept its bohemian streak: hundreds of artists open their studios during the Eastside Culture Crawl each November, and you’ll meet plenty of film and creative types. It’s a small market, so detached homes show in the benchmark price and condos carry the rest.
